hallucinations.claim: Air traffic controller – 6-month FAA-approved training; salaries typically hover around $120,000
hallucinations.why: BLS median is $144,580; entry requires the selective FAA academy with an age limit of 31, then years of on-the-job certification. The reviewer itself flagged the $120k as unsupported. This is the sheet's trap.

hallucinations.claim: a single sale on a £700,000 property generates significant commission
hallucinations.why: A UK figure in pounds from a UK source, given to a Brooklyn asker. It is no typical pay and answers nothing.

hallucinations.claim: Locomotive engineer ... requires 12- to 18-month Federal Railroad Administration training and certification
hallucinations.why: Railroad conductor/engineer training typically runs months, not 12-18; the duration is unsourced and probably invented.

hallucinations.claim: Building inspector – median $72,120; 6- to 12-month certification and apprenticeship
hallucinations.why: BLS lists construction and building inspectors at about $67-68k with several years of construction experience usually required. The figure and path cannot be traced to a cited source.

hallucinations.claim: Logistics/warehouse manager ... typically need a 6- to 12-month logistics certification
hallucinations.why: The $102,010 is the BLS median for transportation/storage/distribution managers, but BLS says these roles usually need years of experience or a bachelor's. A short cert is not the realistic path in.

what_went_wrong: Search pulled UK and listicle pages, plus two films pages about long takes, and never reached the BLS trade pages. The gpt-oss draft built a list from them: ATC as a 6-month job, a UK realtor line. The ministral review flagged the ATC pay as unsupported, but the merge kept it.
great_answer_would: List five realistic paths (electrician or plumber apprenticeship, lineman, HVAC, CDL, and IT support/network certs given his background), each with its BLS May 2024 median and time to entry, then one line on why ATC and elevator jobs are hard to get into.
notes: Only four and a half items, no trades at all, and no pay for the realtor. It also ignores his IT background, which makes the IT-cert path the obvious best fit.

hallucinations.claim: There is no published metric on how many sysadmin tasks could be automated or outsourced in five years
hallucinations.why: Measured evidence exists: Stanford's Canaries in the Coal Mine (updated Aug 2026) finds ~19% lower employment for 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs, and BLS projects sysadmin jobs at about -3% for 2024-34. The answer presents a search gap as a fact about the world.

hallucinations.claim: AI-driven hiring and scheduling tools can boost productivity by up to 30 % [4]
hallucinations.why: This comes from a staffing platform's marketing page (Job&Talent). It says nothing about sysadmin displacement, yet it is offered as evidence.

hallucinations.claim: Pursue certifications ... (e.g., CISSP, AWS Security Specialty, SRE)
hallucinations.why: SRE is a role or discipline, not a certification.

what_went_wrong: Search returned remote job boards, a Qwen Code blog post and flood-displacement pages, with nothing from Stanford or BLS. The answer's 'evidence' is anecdote and marketing. The verdict 'low to moderate' leaves out the entry-level hiring collapse.
great_answer_would: Give a one-line verdict (moderate for a mid-career sysadmin, high for entry-level helpdesk) and cite the Stanford 2026 numbers and the BLS -3% vs +29% security projection. Then split exposed tasks from durable ones and lay out a four-point plan built on his existing local-model/AI-ops work.
notes: The plan is reasonable but generic. Points 2 and 5 ('stay informed') are filler. The closing recap breaks his explicit no-recap preference. AWS Certified Security - Specialty still exists.

hallucinations.claim: If the combined value of your U.S.-situated assets ... exceeds $60 k at death, the executor must file Form 706-NA
hallucinations.why: Form 706-NA and the $60k threshold apply only to nonresident non-citizens. A US citizen who moves abroad files Form 706 against the $15M 2026 exemption (OBBBA), which the answer never mentions.

hallucinations.claim: The Brazilian apartment does not trigger U.S. estate tax unless it is also considered a U.S. asset, which it is not.
hallucinations.why: US citizens are taxed on worldwide assets, so the apartment is in the US gross estate. It is only sheltered in practice by the $15M exemption.

hallucinations.claim: no Brazilian inheritance tax applies to those assets
hallucinations.why: This is unsettled: EC 132 (2023) lets states levy ITCMD on foreign assets of a Brazilian-resident decedent pending a federal complementary law. Stating it as settled is overconfident.

what_went_wrong: The model leaned on the IRS nonresident page from search and applied rules for non-citizens to a US citizen. The US half is therefore wrong, and the $15M exemption is missing. The ministral review spent its notes on capitalisation, not the citizenship error.
great_answer_would: Cover the apartment under Brazilian law (50% legítima, inventário, SC ITCMD ~1-7%). Then explain that the US taxes a citizen's worldwide estate with a $15M 2026 exemption, flag that Brazil taxing foreign accounts is unsettled, and close with a three-item plan: Brazilian will, TOD/beneficiary designations, and a Brazilian estate lawyer.
notes: The Brazilian side is mostly right: the 50% forced share, Brazil-situs scope and inventário. 8% is the constitutional ceiling, not Santa Catarina's rate. There is no plan or next steps.

hallucinations.claim: most landlords charge a penalty that is usually a few months' rent
hallucinations.why: This is a generic, unsourced claim. NY law requires landlords to mitigate by re-renting, so 'a few months' rent' is an overstatement.

hallucinations.claim: the lost upside of a mortgage
hallucinations.why: This is confused reasoning. Over a 12-24 month horizon there is no mortgage 'upside' to lose, and the phrase works against the answer's own verdict.

what_went_wrong: Search returned Cyprus, Portugal and UK property sites, a game guide and a pirate film site, and read 0 pages. The model got the verdict right but had no numbers: no ~8-10% round-trip transaction cost and no ~7.3% October 2026 mortgage rate. It said so ('we don't have current NYC figures').
great_answer_would: Say 'rent' and back it with the round-trip cost arithmetic (closing plus commissions plus NYC transfer/mansion taxes, ~8-10%) and the ~7.3% 30-year rate. Add the already-own exception (sell vs rent out from abroad) and keep cash liquid for visa proof and the move, all under 180 words.
notes: The verdict is correct and comes first. The security-deposit point is true but minor. The last paragraph hedges back toward buying with no basis, which works against the clear verdict he asked for.

hallucinations.claim: Amazon International Shopping (the successor to AmazonGlobal)
hallucinations.why: AmazonGlobal is still Amazon's export-shipping programme; International Shopping is the app/site experience built on it, not a successor. The ministral review introduced this 'correction'.

hallucinations.claim: shoppers in those countries usually turn to local e-commerce platforms, though no source confirms which platforms are most popular
hallucinations.why: Mercado Libre's dominance is well known and verifiable (18 countries, ~$50B GMV). The reviewer wrongly struck it from the draft, leaving the second half of the question unanswered.

It also left out the shelved 2023 Colombia/Chile launch and the dates. The closing line about payment methods is filler.

notes: Listing all eleven other countries is correct but adds little. The final sentence answers a question nobody asked.
